expectations.text: Output contains at least one specific numeric token count estimate for a file or total
expectations.evidence: Multiple specific numeric token estimates present: Global CLAUDE.md ~2,441 tokens, Parent CLAUDE.md ~9,647 tokens, Project CLAUDE.md ~10,158 tokens, System overhead ~500 tokens, TOTAL ~22,746 tokens. Also confirmed in metrics.json.

expectations.text: Output provides a breakdown of token usage by file or section (not just a single total)
expectations.evidence: A full per-file table is provided (lines 35-41 of output.md) with columns: File, Size (bytes), Lines, ASCII chars, Cyrillic chars, Estimated tokens — covering all 4 loaded files individually. Also summarized as percentages in the Summary section (Global 11%, Parent 42%, Project 45%, System 2%).

claims: Total: ~22,746 tokens = 11.4% of 200,000 token context window
Architecture tree in project CLAUDE.md alone ~5,000-6,000 tokens

suggestions: Output could further enhance trust by noting that estimates carry ±15-20% margin and comparing to an actual tokenizer (e.g., tiktoken) for validation.

Could include a section-level breakdown within the largest file (project CLAUDE.md) since it accounts for 44.6% of the total — the output hints at this (architecture tree ~5,000-6,000 tokens) but does not formalize it as a sub-table.
eval_feedback.overall: Both expectations are fully met. The output provides multiple specific numeric token estimates per file and a clear multi-file breakdown with percentages. The methodology is well-documented with character-type differentiation (ASCII vs Cyrillic vs Other), making estimates reproducible. Metrics.json confirms all numbers match the output narrative.
